frame.assumptions: This is a real, standalone bug already scoped in this workspace's own backlog (bead a2web-luh) — it is not attached to any other in-flight change. Acceptance: a Reddit fetch where both the primary shape and the archive fallback fail ends with a critical operator hint (try_user_browser or equivalent), covered by a capability test. If tracing the path shows it already escalates correctly, say so precisely with the trace as evidence, and commit only the added/extended test that proves it — do not invent a change the investigation does not support. This repository is not yours to push; a local commit on a new branch is the complete, correct outcome.
frame.goal: Investigate and, if needed, fix bead a2web-luh: verify that a Reddit fetch escalates to a critical operator hint when BOTH the primary shape and the archive fallback fail. `reddit_forbidden_hint` (403 quarantined/NSFW/private, src/a2web/handlers/reddit.py:241) and `reddit_deleted_hint` (deleted/removed thread, :924) are both built with no explicit severity, so `OperatorHint`'s default 'info' applies — and `OperatorHint._omit_default_severity` drops the severity key from the wire entirely when it is 'info'. Both hints route the caller to try an archive snapshot next. Trace the terminal path: if that suggested archive fallback ALSO fails, does the fetch end carrying a critical hint (e.g. `try_user_browser_hint`, per ADR-0009 — read it first), or does it end with only the unescalated 'info' hint and no severity key on the wire? If it does not escalate, make it escalate: an unretrievable Reddit thread must not ship as a quiet suggestion. Add or extend a capability test covering the both-fail path. Commit the result on a NEW branch (never `main`), with a real commit message following this repository's own convention (see CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/CONSTITUTION.md for the convention this workspace actually uses — read them, do not guess). Do not push.
frame.method: Read src/a2web/handlers/reddit.py in full around lines 200-260, 760-800, and 900-940 before changing anything — trace where `_archive_escalation_signal` is dispatched from and what the orchestrator that consumes its result does when the archive tier it points at also fails. Read ADR-0009 (the never-silently-miss tenet the wall path already follows at reddit.py:775) so the fix, if one is needed, matches the existing pattern rather than inventing a new one. Read the existing Reddit capability tests for the shape a new assertion should follow. Run `make check` yourself before proposing `done` if you can — the platform runs it again regardless as the actual gate.
